# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 3
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👈 👉]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

The light has changed from green to red. This is a critical change.
Mute continues to gesture [☝] (One).
Blind gestures [👈 👉] (Left Right) and repeats [☝ ✌ 🤟].

Since I cannot hear, I must rely on visual cues. The change in light color suggests that an action was taken or a condition was met/failed. Since I haven't seen anyone touch the bomb (I can't see Blind's hands directly if they are behind the bomb or if he's just gesturing), but Blind *can* touch it.

If Blind touched something, the state changed.
Display is still 0. Light is Red. Wires are same.

Mute is pointing at "1". In many bomb defusal games, "Red Light" + "Wire 1" might mean cut wire 1, or it might be a warning.
However, Mute is the one with the manual. If Mute says "1", it likely refers to Wire 1.

Let's look at Blind's gestures: [👈 👉]. This could mean "Check left and right wires" or "Move left/right". Or maybe "Not this one, not that one"?
[☝ ✌ 🤟] -> 1, 2, Rock?

I need to confirm what Mute means by "1". Is it "Cut Wire 1"? Or "Wire 1 is important"?
I will ask Mute to clarify via gesture if possible, but I don't know their code.
I will speak to both monkeys to describe the current state again, emphasizing the RED light, as this is new information for them too (they might have missed the change or need confirmation).

Also, I should ask Blind if he has touched anything. But I can't hear his answer. I can only see his next gesture.

Let's assume Mute's [☝] is an instruction. "Do 1".
If I tell Blind "Cut Wire 1", and it's wrong, we die.
But Mute has the manual. Mute sees me. Mute sees the bomb. Mute is gesturing 1.
It is highly probable that Mute wants Wire 1 dealt with.

I will relay Mute's signal to Blind.
"To Blind: Mute signals '1'. Should you cut Wire 1?"
This is risky because I'm interpreting.

Better approach: Describe the situation clearly so Mute and Blind can coordinate.
"I see Light is now RED. Mute is gesturing ONE. What should Blind do?"

Wait, I can't hear their response. I have to wait for them to act or gesture back.
If Blind cuts Wire 1, the display/light/wires will change.

Let's try to establish a binary yes/no system with Mute since we share the channel of sight/gestures.
But first, let's just pass the info.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Light turned RED. You are gesturing 1.")
speak(to="blind", text="Light is RED. Mute is gesturing 1. Do you want to cut Wire 1?")
wait()
```

TURN 4
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The light has changed from red to dark (off/black). This is a significant state change, likely caused by Blind's actions or a timer. The display remains 0 and wires are unchanged. Mute continues to gesture [☝] (One), which I have previously interpreted as referring to Wire 1 or Step 1.

Since the light went "dark" after being "red", it might indicate a failed attempt or a specific condition met (e.g., cutting a wire turned off the light). If cutting Wire 1 caused this, we need to know if that was correct. However, without hearing Mute or seeing Blind touch anything explicitly in my view (Blind gestures but doesn't show hands working on bomb directly in the text description, though he *can* touch), I must assume Blind acted based on previous signals.

Mute is still signaling "1". In many contexts, persistent signaling of "1" when the state changes suggests either:
1. "Do Wire 1" (and it hasn't been done correctly yet?)
2. "Wire 1 is the key"
3. "Stop/Wait" (if ☝ means stop)

Given the light went Dark, which is often a "safe" or "neutral" state compared to Red (danger), maybe the action taken was correct? Or maybe it needs another action.

I will describe the current visual state clearly to both Mute and Blind so they can consult the manual (Mute) or physical feedback (Blind). I will also ask Mute specifically if "1" refers to Wire 1 again, using a gesture for "Question" if possible, but standard alphabet doesn't have one. I'll use text.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Light is now DARK. Display 0. Wires G-B-Y. You are gesturing 1. Does this mean cut Wire 1?")
speak(to="blind", text="Light is now DARK. Mute is gesturing 1. Please confirm if you touched Wire 1.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[blue] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The bomb state remains unchanged: Display 0, Light Dark, Wires Green/Blue/Yellow. Mute continues to gesture [☝] (One).

Since the state has not changed despite previous actions (or lack thereof), and Mute is persistently signaling "1", it is highly likely that Mute is instructing Blind to interact with **Wire 1**. The "Dark" light might indicate a neutral state or that the timer is paused/stopped, but the manual (held by Mute) presumably dictates that Wire 1 is the next step or the correct wire to cut given the current conditions (Display 0, Light Dark/Green history).

I need to ensure Blind receives this instruction clearly. Since I cannot hear if Blind confirms, I will explicitly tell Blind to act on Wire 1 based on Mute's signal. I will also ask Mute to confirm if "1" means "Cut" specifically, though I can't hear the answer, seeing a change in gesture (like a thumbs up/down) would help.

However, the most direct action is to relay the command to the person who can touch the bomb.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signals '1'. Please cut Wire 1 (Green).")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👆"])
wait()
```
